Podiatrists specialize in foot and ankle conditions. Through physical examinations, imaging, and laboratory tests, they diagnose deformities, injuries, and chronic diseases; provide medication, minimally invasive, and orthotic treatment; operate when necessary; and help patients restore walking and lower-limb function.

paragraphs: A morning can be filled with follow-ups: fitting insoles for flat feet, debriding and dressing diabetic feet, and using a drill on thickened toenails. Around midday, read X-rays to measure bunion angles and schedule surgery. In the afternoon, explain footwear and rehabilitation, write electronic records, and issue prescriptions. Refer difficult cases to orthopedics or vascular medicine and review surgical schedules before leaving.
